issues.description: The problem statement and UML require Animal.messageOnFeed() to return a String (and the tasks specify animal feed messages as String). However, the solution implementation defines Animal.messageOnFeed() to return a FeedResponse object (with Pig and Seal overriding to return FeedResponse as well) and adds a FeedResponse class. This mismatch changes the core method signature students are expected to implement and introduces an extra type not mentioned in the specification or template, which can confuse students and conflict with expected implementations and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the specification by changing Animal.messageOnFeed() and all overrides to return String (containing the feed message). Remove or avoid using the FeedResponse wrapper in the public API, or alternatively update the problem statement and template to explicitly introduce and document FeedResponse as the intended return type and explain its usage so students are aware of the custom type.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Animal.messageOnFeed() returns a String, but the solution changes the concept by making messageOnFeed() return a FeedResponse object (with subclasses returning FeedResponse instances). This introduces a new identifier/concept (FeedResponse) and a different method signature compared to the stated requirement, which can confuse students mapping the requirement (expecting a String message) to the implementation (returning FeedResponse).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type of messageOnFeed() across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to have Animal.messageOnFeed() return String (and have subclasses return the String messages), or (B) update the problem statement and template to explicitly introduce and require a FeedResponse type as the return value. Prefer (A) if the intent is a simple String message as stated in the UML.
